findings.issue: The Convergence Detection list claims review's STOP is gated by "Three binary quality gates (evidence, scope, coverage)". The review stop path evaluates nine legal-stop gates before a candidate becomes STOP — convergenceGate, dimensionCoverageGate, p0ResolutionGate, evidenceDensityGate, hotspotSaturationGate, claimAdjudicationGate, fixCompletenessReplayGate, candidateCoverageGate, graphlessFallbackGate (convergence.cjs:1004-1015); a failed one returns BLOCKED/blockedStop, not a blocked stop of the kind described. The three gates named are a different mechanism: terminal-gates.cjs records the evidence, scope and coverage rows at the terminal stop (:39-41) and a failing row changes the verdict to FAIL, it does not prevent the stop. The same list also omits two review stop conditions the code enforces before those gates: the configured minIterations floor (convergence.cjs:1195-1197, reason minIterationsNotReached) and, under --depth-mode=expansive, the frontierOpen veto that returns CONTINUE while any frontier node is open or active (convergence.cjs:1207-1212), i.e. before any gate is evaluated.

findings.issue: The fan-out spawn step tells the executor to skip "phase_init and phase_main_loop", but this workflow has no phase_main_loop: its phases are phase_init, phase_loop, phase_synthesis and phase_save, so a reader following the instruction looks for a phase key that does not exist. The sibling frontier-seed step and step_reject_extend_with_fanout already state the same fan-out jump with the real names ("never reaches phase_init", "jumps from step_fanout_spawn to phase_synthesis").
